conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you've been having abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting since this morning?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it started around 4 AM. It's sharp and throbbing. I took tramadol and Ativan, but nothing helped.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You haven’t been able to keep anything down, and your last bowel movement was two days ago?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s right. No diarrhea or blood, but I feel really bloated and weak.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to start with IV fluids to help with dehydration and give you some anti-nausea medication.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that sounds good. My blood sugar has probably been high too—I haven’t taken my insulin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your glucose—it’s elevated at 360. We’ll give you insulin through the IV to bring it down safely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had this before—gastroparesis flare. It always hits like this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your history shows chronic gastroparesis. We don’t see signs of infection or blockage on the X-ray, so this looks like another flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: The X-ray was okay? No blockage?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Correct. The bowel gas pattern is normal—no obstruction. We’ll keep monitoring your labs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your latest blood work shows your kidney function is stable—creatinine is 1.2, which is slightly elevated but not concerning right now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that from not drinking? I’ve been so nauseous.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Likely, yes. Dehydration can affect the kidneys temporarily. With fluids, it should improve.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my potassium? I remember last time it was high.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s mildly elevated at 5.6. Because of that, we’re holding your lisinopril for now. It can raise potassium.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I shouldn’t take it at home either?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not until you see your primary doctor. They’ll check your labs and decide when it’s safe to restart.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How’s the pain today? Any improvement?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little better. Still nauseous, but I sipped some broth without vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great progress. We’ll keep advancing your diet slowly—maybe soft foods later today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m worried about my diabetes. My A1c was 10.3—way too high.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your diabetes is not well controlled. We’re continuing your home insulin—Lantus and Humalog—and you’ll need close follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know I need to do better. Stress and pain make it hard to stay on track.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We understand. Managing chronic conditions is tough. Your PCP can help adjust your plan after discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Doctor, I have a bad headache now. It’s pounding on one side.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Could be a migraine. You’re on propranolol, which helps prevent them, but sometimes they still happen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I take sumatriptan? That usually works.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we can give you one dose. But you should avoid taking it with tramadol—there’s a risk of serotonin syndrome.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t know that. I’ve taken them together before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s risky. We’ll prescribe sumatriptan for home use, but please don’t combine it with tramadol or sertraline without checking.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your nausea has improved, and labs are trending better. We think you’re ready to go home today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What about my meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll continue all your usual medications except lisinopril, which stays on hold.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And insulin? I need to adjust it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll stay on Glargine at night and Humalog with meals, plus the sliding scale. Your PCP should see you in 48 hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What if I feel sick again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If vomiting returns or you can’t keep fluids down, come back. Otherwise, focus on small, frequent meals and staying hydrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the headache? Should I see a neurologist?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The sumatriptan helped, right? Keep using it as needed, but avoid tramadol. Your PCP can refer you if migraines continue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll follow up. Thank you for helping me feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and call your doctor if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a final check before discharge. You’re alert, walking fine, and your vitals are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel much better than yesterday. Ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll send your discharge instructions and prescriptions. Remember—no lisinopril, no tramadol with sumatriptan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Safe travels. We’ll see you soon through your PCP.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll make that appointment today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Take care of yourself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for everything.
